old_text:
Manchester City travel to Old Trafford on Sunday seeking to continue their perfect start to life under Enzo Maresca and further prove Anderson's point. The 23-year-old midfielder made his claim upon signing from Nottingham Forest for £116m in the summer and having from afar witnessed City win eight Premier League titles during the past 14 years, compared with United's one.e
"I think Manchester City was unbelievable what they achieved. It's normal when Elliot said that," said Maresca. "If you go back it's a different picture, but for me the reason he said that is because when he grew up Manchester City was dominant."
Panic at Fulham? Not yet, though some distress flares.
Brazilian winger Kevin, an unused substitute against Crystal Palace, added a cryptic message on his Instagram story with the caption 'no speak, no hear, no see'. Alex Iwobi and Emile Smith Rowe have, meanwhile, both cleared their own Instagram posts of football-related content, with some fans interpreting it as growing signs of disharmony within the Fulham camp.
Alvaro Arbeloa moved to calm waters today: ""You can learn more about a group after a defeat than after a win, and I saw them work during the week with a very positive attitude, all of them," the Fulham boss said at a press conference.
"For sure when you are a player and you are not playing, you can't be happy. It is what I expect from the players that are not playing. I want that they should need to show me that they are not happy during the training session. For me, this is the most important thing.
"Obviously, when you are not winning games and you are not helping your team, I think you have more desire to play games and to help their team-mates. But all of them, they have been working so hard and I have a very, very good group with a very good attitude."
Fulham have lost all three league matches this season.
Hull fined over offensive chanting. Anecdotally, you do detect a slight uptick in unpleasant chants from the tiresome edgelord element among clubs' fanbases and Hull have copped a fine for the homophobic antics of some herberts in their support after last season's Cup tie against Chelsea, as Reuters reports:
Hull City have been fined £30,000 ($40,512) by the Football Association over discriminatory chanting during their FA Cup defeat by Chelsea in February, the governing body said on Friday.
An independent regulatory commission also imposed an action plan on the club after it failed to prevent offensive chanting despite warnings over the public address system.
"It was alleged that the club failed to ensure its spectators and/or supporters (and anyone purporting to be supporters) do not use words or behave in an improper, offensive, abusive, indecent or insulting way with a reference - whether express or implied - to sexual orientation," read the statement.
Offensive chanting was heard in sections of the home crowd during the first half of last season's game, prompting an announcement over the PA system urging supporters to stop and reminding them that CCTV was in operation.
A second announcement was made in the second half confirming action had been taken, including arrests made. Hull City have admitted the charges.
Some mid-morning reading: a lovely Moving the Goalposts piece by Tom Garry with Gemma Darvill, coach of the first England women's Parkinson's team and how restorative football has been for her dad, who lives with the condition.
When Gemma Darvill's dad, Les, was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease aged 58, joining a walking football team stopped him from confining himself to his own home, and she believes the game saved his life.
What she could never have foreseen was that, eight years later, she would find herself coaching the first England women's Parkinson's team, helping transform the lives of women with the disease from all across the country. She is set to embark on a journey to Toronto to help spread awareness of the ways in which walking football can help put the brakes on the progression of Parkinson's symptoms.
A teacher at Swallowfield primary school in Woburn Sands, in Milton Keynes, Darvill's interest in walking football was sparked by supporting her dad. She now coaches what is believed to be the first walking football team specifically dedicated to women with Parkinson's, the Parkinson's Pioneers, who train in Solihull and have seen a tenfold increase in their membership in just over three years. That led to her appointment as the coach of the first England women's national side.
And to sign up to Moving the Goalposts, our women's football newsletter, click below:
There's a lot of noise about Manchester United's 15-year-old forward JJ Gabriel, and the volume was ramped up last night when he scored a hat-trick for the U19s in their 5-0 win against Sabah in the Uefa Youth League. Gabriel has already trained with Michael Carrick's first team and his coach Adam Lawrence sung his praises again after Thursday's showing, reports PA.
"JJ is surrounded by people that really, really believe in him from the top of the club right the way through," Lawrence said. "He's been at the club for so long. He's got real good relationships with the players, with the staff, so I think over the course of time obviously that helps as well.
"At the moment, just in terms of his game, his games programme, his training programme, it's about making sure that he's getting the right exposure across different levels. We're obviously not perfect but it's definitely something we put a lot of thought into, so it's good to see him enjoying his football in a good place."
"The first thing is that it's my job is not to ruin him. When you have a talented player like JJ and the other lads, you obviously don't want to stifle their freedom and their creativity.
"What you try and do is to set the team up to allow the talent to function and to play free at the right moments. It can't always be free and off the cuff, in terms of the off-the-ball responsibilities that he's working on and the pressing that he's thinking about.
"But in terms of how he plays properly and how he connects with other team-mates at the top end of the pitch, he's just in a real good space."
Nico O'Reilly is set to return to the Manchester City side for Sunday's derby at Manchester United. The England left-back has missed the last two games after pulling up with a back problem in the warm-up prior to last weekend's Premier League victory over Coventry.
Winger Jeremy Doku remains on the sidelines with the calf problem he sustained in the Community Shield but City have no other fitness concerns for the trip to Old Trafford. The manager, Enzo Maresca, said: "Nico is 100 per cent available but Jeremy, I think he needs some more days." PA
Mikel Arteta has revealed that he likes to set players challenges, such as delaying their meals before matches and making the dressing room hotter, to ensure they are fully prepared for any eventuality.
Arsenal's flight to Italy for their Champions League opener against Napoli this week was delayed for more than five hours, with Arteta forced to cancel his pre-match press conference after the squad arrived in Naples just before 10pm local time. The disruption proved no handicap as they made it 13 successive league-stage victories in Europe, thanks to Martin Ødegaard's second-half winner.
Arteta has a reputation for his innovative methods having previously employed pickpockets during pre-season training camps and preparing for a trip to Anfield by pumping crowd noises through a speaker. The Arsenal manager has now explained how his players have been trained to expect things to go wrong. "I love those challenges. I try to create them in pre-season," he said. "So when they happen, we already experience them and we already know. So, get to the stadium very late, change the routine as soon as the players have to do something else. Because when it happens, and it can happen, you can miss the flight, the train can be delayed, there's so much traffic, and I don't want the players, the staff as well, panicking.
"So, when that happens, adapt to it. 'Okay, we have another two or three hours on the plane, how can we use them?' Play together, spend some time together, sleep, use it, but certainly don't complain and then use it as an excuse because that's not helpful at all."
Asked what other methods he has employed, Arteta added: "Just delay the meals, delay the transport, take a different route. We have done many things: make the dressing room hotter, more difficult, more challenging, less [massage] beds. Those kind of things. Because we are going to have to adapt to different contexts and we will try to anticipate it and create the best possible conditions. But when there is that element of stress or surprise on matchday, it's important [to be prepared]."
João Pedro named Premier League player of the month
Morning everyone. Off to a game this weekend? What are your hopes and expectations? I always aim low in the vague hope of being pleasantly surprised.
Anyway, the season's first monthly awards are in, and João Pedro has been named the Premier League's player of the month for August after registering two goals and two assists in Xabi Alonso's side's swashbuckling start to the season. He's the first Chelsea player to win the award since Cole Palmer in September 2024, fact fans.
The EFL's monthly trinkets are in too, with Southampton's Cyle Larin named Championship player of the month, while Jamal Lowe of Sheffield Wednesday and York's Harry Boyes taking the League One and League Two awards respectively.
The manager awards in the EFL went to Vítor Matos of Swansea (Championship), Huddersfield's Martin Drury (League One) and Dean Brennan of Barnet (League Two).
Thanks Tom. Hull City have confirmed that their winger Sorba Thomas was unhurt following a car accident this morning. After dramatic images were posted on social media, Hull issued a statement saying the Wales winger walked away unscathed.
Hull City is relieved to confirm that Sorba Thomas is unharmed following a road traffic accident near to the club's Cottingham training ground.
The club is aware of images of Sorba's car circulating on social media and can reassure supporters that he has sustained no injuries and emerged from his vehicle completely unscathed.
Matthias Jaissle revealed that summer signing Matias Fernandez-Pardo is edging closer to starting for Newcastle.
The 21-year-old forward arrived on Tyneside from Lille on deadline day and has featured as a substitute in Newcastle's last two matches.
Speaking ahead of Monday's clash with Leeds, Jaissle said: "Yeah, he's getting closer. I said that we need to be smart with his load management. Now he's getting more and more minutes.
"He has now almost a full training week to Leeds, that helps him a lot. I think it's the first time now since he arrived, and then we can make the decision on Sunday, maybe even on Monday." Press Association
Nicolas Jackson is ready to impress, Spurs are scrambled and the 199th Manchester derby takes place at Old Trafford.. here are our 10 things for the upcoming weekend of football:
Spanish World Cup-winner Juan Mata has confirmed he will be departing Australian side Melbourne Victory, but stopped short of calling time on his career.
The former Manchester United and Chelsea ace has enjoyed a late-career resurgence and was voted the domestic A-League player of the year in 2025-26.
But the 38-year-old has decided not to play on at the club as he mulls "the next steps in his career".
He will remain involved with the Australian side after taking an ownership stake.
"I loved every minute and so greatly enjoyed everything that we achieved last season, falling back in love with football at such a special place, in an amazing city that it was a privilege to call home," Mata said.
"Now I am excited about our next chapters, believing together in the future of Australian football and inspiring the next generation of Melbourne Victory players and supporters." AFP
Gianni Infantino has not responded to a request to appear before the US House judiciary committee or sent documents requested by one of its members more than a month past the deadline.
The Democrat Jamie Raskin, the ranking minority member of the committee, wrote to the Fifa president on 26 July informing the Swiss he was launching an investigation into "a sustained campaign" by Fifa to curry favour with the US president, Donald Trump.
His letter said seeking of favours extended to the dismissal of high-profile corruption cases, while also accusing Fifa of "gouging" American consumers with "exorbitant" World Cup ticket prices this summer.
The Swiss was asked to respond to the letter by 9 August with the requested documents and to make contact with the committee to schedule an interview, but it is understood no response at all had been received as of Thursday.
Because no subpoena was issued, there are no criminal consequences for ignoring Raskin's request. Press Association
In totally normal Turkish football news... the Fenerbahce head coach, Ismail Kartal, announced his resignation on Thursday after his team drew 1-1 at home to Roma in the Champions League - but minutes later, the club president said Kartal would stay in the job.
Kartal shocked the post-match press conference by claiming he was leaving Fenerbahce "never to return". The 65-year-old added that he was taking the drastic decision "to clear the way for the club" - but the Fenerbahce president, Aziz Yildrim, quickly moved to play down his manager's remarks.
Minutes after the press conference, Yildirim told reporters that Kartal "continues in his role" with the Turkish side. "Some fans threw a bottle at the coach's head this evening during the game. He is upset about it," the club president added.
The French football federation's president, Philippe Diallo, said Gianni Infantino had "seriously damaged the image and the unity of football" as he announced the end of France's support for the Fifa president's re-election.
The FFF's executive committee unanimously voted on Thursday to withdraw its backing, which had been formalised at the end of June. Diallo referred to "events during the World Cup" which had "flagrantly gone against the way we believe our sport should be run" and to Infantino's World Cup sell-off plan, which was revealed in July and scrapped after a widespread backlash.
United were the only Premier League club in Champions League action last night but Englishman Harry Kane scored for the eighth game in a row in the competition as Bayern Munich beat Bodø/Glimt 5-0 at the Allianz Arena. Starting their Champions League journey were Cesc Fabregas's Como, who beat RB Leipzig 4-1 Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia, while Lens scored twice in added time to reverse a 2-1 deficit and secure a 3-2 win. Our roundup of all of Thursday night's European action is here.
Manchester United were back in Europe's elite competition after a two-year hiatus and in need of something to soothe them after the trauma of their last-gasp coughing up of two points in last Sunday's Premier League draw at Everton. And before the extremely serious business of the derby here against Manchester City on Sunday. They got it on the back of a first-half performance that burned slowly before catching fire.
Sabah were game. United were clinical. It was Matheus Cunha who broke the deadlock midway through the first half and the defining moments came at the end of the period when Bruno Fernandes and Benjamin Sesko sent United into half-time with a three-goal cushion. Lisandro Martínez added the fourth late on. It was a case of job done for Michael Carrick, no wobbles. Now for City.
Read David Hytner's full report from Old Trafford:
Newcastle United defender Lewis Hall has signed a new long-term contract with the club.
Reports suggest the left-back, 22, has agreed a two-year extension to his original deal that would take his contract up to 2031.
Hall has been the subject of interest from Manchester United, among others, but has now committed his immediate future to Newcastle.
"It's an absolute pleasure to play for this club and to represent the supporters," he said. "I know how much it means to them.
"To be able to bring joy to their faces, it's a big thing for me. I obviously have a family connection with the club, which is incredibly important to us all.
"One of the main reasons I play is to make my family proud, and I know how much it means to them to watch me playing for Newcastle United."
No club embraces chaos quite like Chelsea. Stability has been absent at Stamford Bridge going back even as far as the Ken Bates era. The latest twist in west London has been foreseen for a while, with warring factions between the current ownership meaning a parting of ways was always likely but Mark Walter's issues with US tax authorities have accelerated the timeline. Then, on Thursday evening, Matt Hughes and Jacob Steinberg came through with the report that Chelsea's majority owners, Clearlake Capital, are closing in on an agreement to buy out co-owners Todd Boehly and Walter in a deal that would see the pair make a profit on their investment and value the club at around £5bn.
We'll be across any further updates on that story, plus the reaction to last night's European action and all the other news ahead of the weekend football. Plenty to get stuck into.
new_text:
Andy Hunter spoke to Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall, a player from the Everton School of Science.
"I get where people are coming from; everyone wants to sign everyone and have the perfect squad. But there are still 19 lads in this building who are going to hopefully take this club to good things this year. That was getting disregarded.
"I saw people saying: 'We'll be lucky to stay up this year.' What message is that sending to the lads who are already here? I'm not blaming anyone. We get it. It didn't work. But let's all be positive - right, it's done, bang, let's go - and that's what we've been trying to say in the dressing room. Of course we would have wanted to sign a couple more, but we're happy with what we've got and it's given us more impetus now to move on."
Via Sky News' Rob Harris: Gianni Infantino has announced his Fifa re-election slogan:
"Football belongs to everyone, everywhere in the world."
The bumph continues: "We want to give everyone the opportunity to dream, to participate... to narrow the gap between the big and all the others & that's what I will continue to be doing."
Rangers news: Dan Purdy is to step down from his role as technical director.
A statement on Rangers' website read: "We can confirm today that Dan Purdy will step down from his position as technical director. Dan will continue to work with the club's ownership group, supporting the transition and other football projects. The board would like to thank Dan for his commitment and contribution during his time at Rangers and wishes him every success for the future."
Fifa have imposed life bans on two former soccer federation presidents for financial misconduct, including one who stayed in office since being sanctioned in 2011 as part of a notorious election bribery scandal in the Caribbean.
Montserrat's long-time soccer leader Vincent Cassell was charged with "abuse of position, systemic conflicts of interest" and misuse of Fifa and federation funds, Fifa said in a statement on Friday.
The former president of the Maldives soccer federation, Bassam Adeel Jaleel, was expelled from the sport for "misusing Fifa Covid-19 Relief Plan funds for his personal benefit," FIFA said. During the pandemic in 2020 Fifa said it would make up to $1.5 billion available in grants and loans.
Maldives media reported this year that Jaleel was sentenced to 23 years in prison for embezzling $1.2 million from Fifa. The money was intended for local soccer clubs and was reportedly used to buy apartments.
Both Cassell and Jaleel, who was elected like Infantino in 2016, were presidents of their federations the next year during the Fifa congress in Bahrain. Infantino told his audience in a keynote speech in Manama, "We don't want you," if they were corrupt.
"If there's anyone in this room or outside of this room who still thinks he can enrich himself," Infantino said in 2017, "that he can abuse football, I have one clear and strong message to tell him: Leave football and leave football now."
Lamine Camara was the midfielder who got away from Chelsea but he now says he's focused on playing for Monaco.
The deal was suddenly scrapped when Everton reversed its decision on Folarin Balogun and attempted to get that signing done. In the end, neither player moved and both are still at the French club.
"There was a possibility I could leave. It didn't go through at the last minute and that's part of football," Camara said. Monaco play Strasbourg on Saturday. "I've turned the page and am focusing on the season."
"It's part of a professional player's life. I managed to stay professional and not dwell on it too much," he said. "Once it's happened there's no point in thinking about it again."
The battle over who will host the 2030 World Cup final has intensified after Morocco's prime minister told his country's football federation head to stop making promises before the Spanish FA chief insisted it should be held in Spain.
Moroccan PM Aziz Akhannouch took aim at Royal Moroccan Football Federation (RMFF) President Fouzi Lekjaa, who boldly declared at a political party event that Casablanca would have the "honour" of hosting the final.
Fifa have not yet announced which of the three co-hosts - Spain, Portugal or Morocco - will host the final in 2030, with a spokesperson saying a decision would be made in due course. "Do not offer to host the big final game in Morocco while we still have not discussed the matter with our allies, Spain and Portugal. There should be some respect, brothers," Akhannouch said at a rally ahead of elections later this month. "Stop using electoral promises to pull the rug out from under us. These are huge matters. Deciding where the final will be held is a major issue."
More De Zerbi on Tottenham's winless start: "We are better than last season. We are not winning and we are not scoring, but I am positive because I believe in my players and this group. The players have big qualities and potential. We are working well. I am not happy because I suffer from defeats and when we don't score, but I am experienced enough to see improvement."
Roberto De Zerbi has been speaking about Richarlison's future, with the Brazilian not included in Tottenham's Premier League squad: ""I don't know. It's not my job. What I can say, is that I know very well what the club has done for Richarlison, and very well what Richarlison has done for the club in the last two months. I know, he knows, the club knows, his agent knows. Everyone knows, better than you [the media]. Much better."
Peter Oh gets in touch: "I for one find Mikel Arteta's psychological tricks as cringe-inducing as Brendan Rodgers' three envelopes stunt when he was at Liverpool. If he really wants his players to overcome challenges, how about paying them normal people's wages for a season?"
Liverpool commemorate Matt Beard with memorial garden
Ahead of the first anniversary of his passing, a private ceremony was held at the club's training ground for players, staff and Matt Beard's family, where a memorial garden in his name - which will provide a quiet space for reflection and remembrance - was officially unveiled.
This was followed by the planting of a commemorative tree in his honour on 97 Avenue, outside Anfield, creating a permanent place where fans can visit and remember Beard.
Beard was women's manager from 2012 to 2015 and again from 2021 to 2025. Under his leadership, the Reds won back-to-back Women's Super League titles in 2013 and 2014, before securing promotion to the Women's Super League with the FA Women's Championship title in 2022.
Liverpool have joined other clubs in supporting the Premier League's 'Together Against Suicide' initiative, to raise awareness of suicide prevention and remind people that support is available.
Brentford visit Bournemouth on Saturday, with Keith Andrews backing Brazil striker Igor Thiago to get back on the Premier League goal trail: "The goals will come, I've no doubt about that. I'm not worried about that and he's performing to a really high level for us."
Thiago got 25 last season but has scored just once this season, and that against Birmingham in the Carabao Cup.
Football Daily has landed, and is on that irrepressible prankster Mikel Arteta:
The use of psychological stratagems and pitchside or locker-room sabotage has long been employed by football managers trying to give their teams an edge over visiting rivals. Whether it's placing the pegs too high or the seats too low, painting the walls an aggression-lowering shade of pink or deliberately moving the advertising hoardings to prevent long throws, there are apparently no stones conniving coaching staff will leave unturned if they think their team's chances of winning may be improved by such shenanigans. Almost 40 years ago, Wimbledon's Crazy Gang famously used to leave visitors to Plough Lane without any hot water, a plan that seemed stunning in its simplicity, until you realise - as Football Daily has just done after nearly 40 years - that footballers generally tend not to shower until after the game is over, rendering their attempt at disruption decidedly redundant.
A man who has previously attracted ridicule for hiring a team of pickpockets to pinch his players' watches, phones and wallets during a team dinner to teach them the value of vigilance and focus, it ought to come as no surprise that Mikel Arteta has now hit upon the psychological wheeze of disrupting his own team's preparations for matches as a way of keeping them on their toes. The Arsenal manager has revealed that he occasionally has dressing-room thermostats turned up to 11, delays meal and transport times, or has physio room massage beds "disappeared" to ensure Arsenal's finest are prepared for any curveballs life might pitch their way. And while such half-baked amateur psychology will almost certainly provide more grist to the mill of Arteta haterz, if inducing mild anxiety in Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka over a toasty canteen or slightly late bus is all it takes to finally win a league title, then who are we to carp?
Some interesting transfer news from the Championship. Michail Antonio has returned to English football to join Watford on a one-year deal. The former West Ham forward had been with Al Sailiya SC in Qatar but has not played in England since being injured in a horrific car accident in December 2024. The 36-year-old might even be in the bench for Saturday's match against Stoke at Vicarage Road.
One of the most eye-catching matches in Europe this weekend is Elversberg's home Bundesliga match against Bayern Munich on Sunday afternoon, and the good news for the top flight newcomers is that their coach, Vincent Wagner, has been cleared to be in the dug-out after the referee of last week's win over Borussia Mönchengladbach admitted making a mistake in sending him off.
The team from a town of only 13,000 people have made a stunning start to life in the Bundesliga, beating Bayer Leverkusen and Mönchengladbach.
Wagner was due to sit out the big Bayern clash but his one-game ban was overturned on appeal on Friday after referee Martin Petersen made an admission of an error.
Stephan Oberholz, chair of the German federation's tribunal, said Petersen admitted he got it wrong when he showed Wagner a second yellow card as the coach walked on to the field at halftime. Oberholz said the referee now accepted Wagner hadn't been trying to confront him and had instead been heading toward his own players.
More developments in today's twistiest, turniest story - Fenerbace are now reported to have accepted coach Ismail Kartal's resignation, having earlier insisted he would be carrying on despite announcing he was quitting after last night's Champions League draw with Roma. Here's AP's latest:
Fenerbahce have accepted coach Ismail Kartal's resignation on Friday, Turkish media reports said, after failing to convince him to stay at the helm of the Istanbul side.
Kartal announced he was stepping down following Thursday's draw against Roma in a Champions League game. He did not explain why he was quitting just three months after taking up the position and refused to take questions.
Fenerbahce initially refused to accept his resignation following the 1-1 draw in Istanbul but failed to persuade him to stay, NTV television and other media reported. Assistant coach Dirk Kuyt would temporarily manage the team, the report said. There was no immediate official statement from Fenerbahce.
David Moyes speaks. And he sas that Jack Grealish might be ready to start for Everton at Tottenham, who have only 17 players available for the trip to north London. "Jack's a special case and I think he is ready to play from the start - he is a boy who needs the football more than he needs the training but he's still building up to his best. He's incredibly exciting if he gives us what he gave us at the start of last season."
Moyes added that Everton might still dip into the free transfer market having endured a frustrating summer window but it wouldn't deliver exactly what he needs. "Having a bigger squad helps if anything goes wrong - we're looking in the free transsfer market and to see if there's players out there but to get players at the level we're at will not be easy."
Thank you, Mr JB. Afternoon everyone. To Scotland, and the first Old Firm meeting of the season, in the League Cup quarter-finals at Ibrox on Sunday, which will lack some of its usual bite due to away fans being, predictably, banned again following some equally predictable naughtiness between the two sets of fans when they met in the Scottish Cup in March. Here's PA's take:
Martin O'Neill revealed Celtic were given a "general behaviour" warning by Police Scotland ahead of Sunday's Premier Sports Cup quarter-final against Rangers at Ibrox.
There will be no Hoops fans in the 50,000-capacity stadium at the order of the authorities amid a ticket allocation spat between the two Glasgow giants. The spat is partly a result of the last Old Firm clash in Govan in March, which was marred by fans' disorder as Celtic won the Scottish Gas Scottish Cup quarter-final on penalties after a goalless 120 minutes.
The two clubs have both been ordered to play their next home Scottish Cup matches behind closed doors and have also been handed a £100,000 compensation bill, paid to whichever team is drawn as the away side in their next respective fixtures in that competition. The 74-year-old Hoops boss admitted that "it'll be a bit strange not having the (Celtic) fans in but I'm nervously and excitedly looking forward to it, it's a great fixture" and also spoke about the police visit.
O'Neill said: "We had the police come in today, just a little 15 minute meeting with us, just reminders of our behaviour, which I think is actually a timely reminder. It a good thing as well. I think it's the overall picture. Gosh, it'd be nice to have something to celebrate. I think it's just general behaviour from us.
"They didn't mention this but I would have assumed that one of the things that they considered is what happens on the field of play, because these things can be taken further. You don't want any sort of punch-ups for a start, secondly, you don't want too excessive celebrations, stuff like that, if that was the case.
"I mean, I'd be delighted to be celebrating something in the game. But it's the behaviour in the light of what has happened in recent fixtures."
And the sides meet again on Sunday week in the league, this time at Celtic Park.
Bournemouth v Brentford on Saturday, with Marco Rose looking for his first league win; his team beat Lincoln in the Carabao Cup. "It's important and I would love to have it done already but it's not the case.
"We need to work for it. We have to stick together, we have to believe in it. If you start a season, if you win your first game, it's like, 'OK, now we can go', so we need to do it. I think a home game with our fans is a big chance to do it and always the next game is a chance to change things, to change situations. We are quite confident."
It's been two draws and a defeat so far. Both the Everton and Newcastle games saw Rose's team pegged back.
Russell Martin corner. He's been talking about the ownership of Leicester, the club on open sale: "I don't know if the club is up for sale completely I don't know when the deadline is. It's not my job to know any of that really. I think Khun Top, Jon [Rudkin] and the guys, we spoke a lot over the transfer window and they've supported us hugely.
"He's [the owner] still hugely invested in the club, otherwise we wouldn't have signed 14 players and tried to rebuild the energy and team at this club that will hopefully bring success. So as long as everyone's really supportive of that and we're all open lines of communication, which it has been, then we'll have to wait and see on the other stuff."
Andrew Beasley has run the numbers on this week's Champions League action.
Despite 16 of the 18 matches being won, there were no shocks. For the bloated league phase to generate serious excitement, it needs major upsets. Only two wins were secured by the underdog according to bookmakers, and one of those was Europa League champions Aston Villa beating Club Brugge. Hardly an upset when you compare their finances.
Xabi Alonso dead-batted questions of the changing Chelsea ownership: "I'm not the guy to give you information about those things. Nothing I have and not my knowledge. I'm working fine, I'm very happy with how we have started and how we are working together aligned and this is all I can say at the moment."
Further detail from that Chelsea story on the departure of Enzo Fernandez: "Neto's determination to stay contrasted with the stance of Enzo Fernández, who was sold to City for £125m during the closing hours of the transfer window.
"He was not handed a new contract after initial discussions were held. The Argentina midfielder raised questions over his future in March, criticising January's departure of Enzo Maresca as head coach and sparking talk of a move to Real Madrid by expressing a desire to live in the Spanish capital. Chelsea responded by banning Fernández for two games.
"Madrid downplayed their interest in Fernández but the 25-year-old continued to push for a new challenge. City, who appointed Maresca as Pep Guardiola's replacement, emerged as Fernández's strongest suitors. Football Daily has landed, and is on that irrepressible prankster Mikel Arteta: The use of psychological stratagems and pitchside or locker-room sabotage has long been employed by football managers trying to give their teams an edge over visiting rivals. Whether it's placing the pegs too high or the seats too low, painting the walls an aggression-lowering shade of pink or deliberately moving the advertising hoardings to prevent long throws, there are apparently no stones conniving coaching staff will leave unturned if they think their team's chances of winning may be improved by such shenanigans. AFP Gianni Infantino has not responded to a request to appear before the US House judiciary committee or sent documents requested by one of its members more than a month past the deadline. The Democrat Jamie Raskin, the ranking minority member of the committee, wrote to the Fifa president on 26 July informing the Swiss he was launching an investigation into "a sustained campaign" by Fifa to curry favour with the US president, Donald Trump. His letter said seeking of favours extended to the dismissal of high-profile corruption cases, while also accusing Fifa of "gouging" American consumers with "exorbitant" World Cup ticket prices this summer. The Swiss was asked to respond to the letter by 9 August with the requested documents and to make contact with the committee to schedule an interview, but it is understood no response at all had been received as of Thursday. Because no subpoena was issued, there are no criminal consequences for ignoring Raskin's request. Press Association In totally normal Turkish football news... the Fenerbahce head coach, Ismail Kartal, announced his resignation on Thursday after his team drew 1-1 at home to Roma in the Champions League - but minutes later, the club president said Kartal would stay in the job. Kartal shocked the post-match press conference by claiming he was leaving Fenerbahce "never to return". The 65-year-old added that he was taking the drastic decision "to clear the way for the club" - but the Fenerbahce president, Aziz Yildrim, quickly moved to play down his manager's remarks. Minutes after the press conference, Yildirim told reporters that Kartal "continues in his role" with the Turkish side. "Some fans threw a bottle at the coach's head this evening during the game. He is upset about it," the club president added. The French football federation's president, Philippe Diallo, said Gianni Infantino had "seriously damaged the image and the unity of football" as he announced the end of France's support for the Fifa president's re-election. The FFF's executive committee unanimously voted on Thursday to withdraw its backing, which had been formalised at the end of June. Diallo referred to "events during the World Cup" which had "flagrantly gone against the way we believe our sport should be run" and to Infantino's World Cup sell-off plan, which was revealed in July and scrapped after a widespread backlash.
